prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1274; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed head-on collision. The insured driver reports the other vehicle crossed into their lane, and the claimant is represented by counsel who has requested that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is named on it and was covered on the date of the loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 3: Inspected the vehicle and photographed the front-end damage. The damage pattern matches the impact as described, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior records.

Entry 4: Police report and statements from the scene confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Photos from the scene confirm some details of the account, although no independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 5: The claimant's medical records report whiplash. The reported injury is plausible for a crash of this severity. Records also show a small strain in the same area several years ago that healed fully, so the prior history has been noted.

Entry 6: Counsel supplied a supplemental statement with some added details. The core account has not changed from the original report, and the additions are minor and consistent with it.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved. Based on the records, the file is moving toward a reasonable evaluation of the injury claim, with ongoing review of the treatment notes.
